verdict_text: Histogram boosting clears the absolute-direction bar set before the run. On the 20-session top 10 its walk-forward interval sits above the share of liquid names that were up, the holdout is above its own base rate, and at least seven walk-forward years agree. The equal-weight composite and the logistic do not clear that bar. The same boosting slate beats SPY on 40.9% of walk-forward picks against a 47.0% universe rate, and on 46.5% of holdout picks against 47.4%. A non-overlapping 20-session top-10 book finishes at 1.32 times capital over the walk-forward, against 3.30 for SPY and 1.07 for random slates. The holdout book finishes at 0.91, against 1.14 for SPY. There is not a robust edge over SPY. Being up more often than the average stock is not the same as beating the market, and the compounded book does not finish ahead of SPY in both samples. The average net return is also much larger than the median, so a few very large winners carry the mean.
